subtitle: When the Hand of Ritual Became the Hand of Rule

panels.shot: dramatic split-scene wide, half showing a young Mayurasharma with palm-leaf manuscript and sacrificial fire, half showing him later in armour with unsheathed sword against the forests of Sriparvata
panels.action: On one side, young Mayurasharma in simple Brahmin robes clutches a palm-leaf book beside a quiet altar; on the other, an older Mayurasharma in mail and crown grips a drawn sword before thick Western Ghats forests and the distant town of Banavasi.

dialogue.text: In an age when Brahmins sought the fire-altar, Mayurasharma of Talagunda walked to Kanchi, quarreled with a Pallava horseman, and returned as Mayuravarman, founding a forest kingdom in Kannada land.

i18n.hi: जब ब्राह्मण यज्ञाग्नि खोजते थे, तब तलगुंड के मयूरशर्मा कांची तक चले, एक पल्लव घुड़सवार से भिड़े, और मयूरवर्मन बन लौटे, कन्नड देश के अरण्यों में राज्य बसाने।

panels.shot: slow push-in from sky over Western Ghats down onto Talagunda village nestled by fields and a small shrine
panels.action: From above, mist curls over the dark folds of the Western Ghats as the view drops to the modest settlement of Talagunda; in the foreground, young Mayurasharma watches priests at a village shrine, eyes intent, palm-leaf bundle under his arm.

dialogue.text: Before he was king, he was a village boy of Talagunda, of the Manavya lineage, where muddy fields met old stones and the names of Vedic seers were still spoken at dawn.

i18n.hi: राजा बनने से पहले, वह तलगुंड का गाँव का लड़का था, मानव्य कुल का, जहाँ कीचड़भरे खेत प्राचीन शिलाओं से मिलते थे और भोर में अभी भी वैदिक ऋषियों के नाम गूंजते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level of Mayurasharma seated before his teacher, with forests and hills behind
panels.action: Mayurasharma kneels respectfully before an unseen elder guru, hands folded, with thick bamboo groves and distant hill outlines behind them, his simple thread across his chest catching the light.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda pillar remembers him first not as a fighter but as a student, setting out with his teacher Veerasharma, leaving the cool shade of his home groves for a fiercer light.

i18n.hi: तलगुंड स्तंभ उसे पहले योद्धा नहीं, विद्यार्थी मानता है, जो गुरु वीरशर्मा संग निकला, अपने शीतल उपवनों की छाया छोड़ किसी और ही तेज रोशनी की ओर।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of a long road leading east towards Kanchipuram with caravans and pilgrims
panels.action: On a dusty eastern road, Mayurasharma walks barefoot beside his guru’s bullock cart, sharing the path with traders, pilgrims, and soldiers, as distant temple towers rise faintly against the horizon.

dialogue.text: They walked east towards Kanchi, the Pallava capital, where a great ghatika called the learned from far lands, to drink Veda and grammar in the shelter of royal power.

i18n.hi: वे कांची की ओर चले, पल्लव राजधानी, जहाँ एक महान घाटिका दूर–दूर के पंडितों को बुलाती थी, ताकि वे राजशक्ति की छाया में वेद और व्याकरण का रस पी सकें।

panels.shot: high-angle wide shot of Kanchipuram city with walls, temples, and the ghatika complex bustling with students
panels.action: The bustling city of Kanchipuram spreads below, with walls, markets, and tall temple towers; within a walled monastery courtyard, young men in simple robes debate under colonnades while Mayurasharma enters, awed.

dialogue.text: Kanchi was no village shrine but a world-city, its ghatika a humming hive of recitation and argument, supported by the Pallava kings whose horsemen and ministers watched from nearby barracks.

i18n.hi: कांची कोई गाँव का देवालय नहीं, एक जग-नगर था; उसकी घाटिका जप और बहस का गुंजारता छत्ता, जिसे पल्लव राजाओं का धन, घुड़सवार और अमात्य पास के छावनियों से देखते रहते।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of the ghatika courtyard with Mayurasharma in study among other Brahmin students
panels.action: In a shaded hall, Mayurasharma sits cross-legged among other students, reciting from a palm-leaf manuscript while his guru listens, the faint silhouette of an armed Pallava guard visible through an open doorway.

dialogue.text: The inscription praises his eagerness for sacred learning, yet we are told another presence shared this space of syllables and rules: the mounted power of the Pallavas themselves.

i18n.hi: लेख उसकी पवित्र विद्या की लालसा की प्रशंसा करता है, पर बताता है कि इस अक्षर–लोक में एक और छाया भी थी: खुद पल्लवों की घुड़सवार शक्ति।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide in the ghatika outer courtyard showing a Pallava horseman and Mayurasharma in tense confrontation
panels.action: In the outer courtyard, a Pallava horseman in armour, hand on his horse’s reins, leans forward in harsh argument with Mayurasharma, who stands rigid, fists clenched at his sides, other students watching from a distance.

dialogue.text: One day, the Talagunda pillar recalls, there was a fierce quarrel between this scholar and a Pallava horseman; the words are lost, but not the wound they left on his pride.

i18n.hi: एक दिन, तलगुंड स्तंभ के अनुसार, इस विद्वान और एक पल्लव घुड़सवार के बीच भयंकर झगड़ा हुआ; शब्द खो गए, पर उसकी मान पर लगे घाव की टीस बची रही।

panels.shot: tight medium on Mayurasharma’s face turned slightly away from the horseman, capturing humiliation, anger, and thought
panels.action: Close on Mayurasharma’s face as he turns slightly from the mounted man, jaw set, eyes burning more with hurt than rage, the shadow of the horse’s head falling across his shoulder.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers added slaps, torn garments, barred ceremonies; the stone itself stays silent on such blows, but it remembers the quarrel and what it awakened in him.

i18n.hi: बाद के किस्सागो slaps, फटी धोती, रोकी गई पूजा जोड़ते हैं; पत्थर ऐसे थप्पड़ों पर चुप है, पर झगड़े को और उसमें जागी आग को नहीं भूलता।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Mayurasharma leaving the ghatika gate carrying his few belongings, with the city behind
panels.action: Mayurasharma walks away from the ghatika gate, a small bundle of palm leaves and a staff on his shoulder, the high walls and towers of Kanchi looming behind him as he does not look back.

dialogue.text: Whatever the exact insult, it was enough. The Brahmin from Talagunda turned from the safety of the ghatika and chose the open road, carrying not just books but a sharpened resolve.

i18n.hi: अपमान कुछ भी रहा हो, काफी था। तलगुंड का ब्राह्मण घाटिका की सुरक्षा छोड़कर खुली राह पर उतरा, साथ सिर्फ पुस्तकें नहीं, धारदार संकल्प भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of dense Sriparvata forested hills with Mayurasharma entering the treeline
panels.action: A rugged line of forested hills rises ahead, clouds snagging their peaks; in the foreground, Mayurasharma steps into the deep shade of the Sriparvata woods, staff in hand, his figure small against the towering trees.

dialogue.text: The prashasti says he entered the forests of Sriparvata, not as an outlaw but as one who had traded altar for arms, seeking a new path between the city’s riders and his own hurt honour.

i18n.hi: प्रशस्ती कहती है वह श्रीपर्वत के अरण्यों में घुसा, डाकू बन नहीं, बलि छोड़ शस्त्र उठाने वाला, शहर के सवारों और अपनी आहत इज्जत के बीच नई राह खोजता हुआ।

panels.shot: mid-wide inside the forest, with Mayurasharma practicing with a spear or sword improvised from a staff, alone
panels.action: Within the dense forest clearing, shafts of light fall on Mayurasharma as he grips a long staff like a spear, body low and focused, practicing thrusts and parries against the shadows of trees.

dialogue.text: There, among rocks and vines, the man of mantra trained his limbs. The Talagunda poets would later say that anger, once kindled, drove him to seize the kshatra, the duty of rule and defence.

i18n.hi: वहाँ, शिलाओं और लताओं के बीच, मंत्रों का आदमी अंग–प्रशिक्षण करने लगा। तलगुंड कवि बाद में लिखेंगे कि भड़की हुई क्रोध–अग्नि ने उसे क्षत्रधर्म, राज और रक्षा, थामने को धकेला।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mayurasharma meeting local forest chieftains or men, suggesting alliances without showing battle
panels.action: In a forest hamlet, Mayurasharma stands speaking earnestly to rugged local chieftains, one with a bow, another with a plough, while beyond them the terrain drops towards plains and distant settlements.

dialogue.text: The record is brief, but its meaning is heavy: he gathered strength in these hills, winning allies among those who knew the tracks and streams, turning a scholar’s clarity into a leader’s plan.

i18n.hi: लेख छोटा है, पर अर्थ भारी: इन पहाड़ियों में उसने बल जोड़ा, पगडंडियाँ और धाराएँ जानने वालों को अपना बना, और विद्वान की दृष्टि को सेनानी की योजना में बदला।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of the frontier region between Pallava territory and the western forests, showing patrols and watchtowers
panels.action: From above, sparse Pallava watchtowers and small garrisons dot the borderlands, their banners fluttering, while beyond them the thick forest line hints at a world beyond royal reach.

dialogue.text: The Pallavas’ strength lay in cities and cavalry, but their grasp thinned westward; beyond their watchtowers lay older forest communities, where a determined newcomer could carve out space for himself.

i18n.hi: पल्लवों की ताकत नगरों और घुड़सवारों में थी, पर पश्चिम की ओर उनकी पकड़ ढीली पड़ती; चौकियों के परे पुराने वनसमुदाय थे, जहाँ जिद्दी नवागंतुक खुद के लिए जगह तराश सकता था।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of Mayurasharma confronting a small Pallava detachment in a tense standoff, weapons drawn but no violence shown
panels.action: On a rugged track, Mayurasharma, now armed and flanked by his followers, faces a small Pallava detachment, both sides with weapons drawn but held, the wind catching their banners as they size one another up.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda inscription hints at war with Pallava forces, not with gory detail but with proud phrases: that he broke their power in the forests and forced their hand to recognize his own.

i18n.hi: तलगुंड शिलालेख पल्लव सेना से युद्ध की ओर इशारा करता है; रक्तरंजित कथा नहीं, गर्वीले वाक्य: कि उसने अरण्यों में उनकी शक्ति तोड़ी और उन्हें अपना अधिकार मानने पर मजबूर किया।

panels.shot: mid-wide of a formal meeting or truce scene between Mayurasharma’s envoys and Pallava officials, suggesting recognition
panels.action: Within a simple hall, Mayurasharma stands opposite dignified Pallava officials; hands are extended in measured agreement, while a map or palm-leaf grant lies between them, guarded soldiers watching in composed silence.

dialogue.text: They did not call him outlaw; the poetic stone says the Pallavas, pressed by his resistance, granted him the right to rule these western lands, turning a quarrel into a negotiated frontier.

i18n.hi: उसे डकैत नहीं कहा गया; काव्य–शिला कहती है पल्लव, उसकी जिद से दबकर, इन पश्चिमी भूभागों पर शासन का अधिकार उसे दे बैठे, झगड़े को समझौते वाली सीमा में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: ceremonial low-angle shot of Mayurasharma being anointed or seated as ruler in Banavasi, with local elites present
panels.action: In an open courtyard at Banavasi, Mayurasharma sits on a simple raised seat being anointed by Brahmin elders, local chiefs standing by with respect, while villagers watch, the forested hills visible beyond the settlement.

dialogue.text: So the man once known as Mayurasharma took a new seat and a new title, rooted now at Banavasi, a frontier town that would become the heart of his Kadamba line.

i18n.hi: इस तरह, जो कभी मयूरशर्मा था, उसने नया आसन और नया उपाधि ली, अब बनवासी में जड़ें जमाकर, वह सीमा–नगर जो उसकी कदंब वंश का हृदय बनेगा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Mayurasharma holding a sword in one hand and a manuscript in the other, with attendants around
panels.action: Mayurasharma stands at the edge of a pillared hall, a sword resting in one hand and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript in the other, attendants behind him, his expression calm yet firm.

dialogue.text: The Gudnapur and Talagunda stones agree: this king traced his birth to Brahmins, yet bore the new suffix varman, asserting kshatriya duty through political claim rather than some neat ritual of conversion.

i18n.hi: गुडनपुर और तलगुंड दोनों पत्थर मानते हैं: यह राजा जन्म से ब्राह्मण था, पर उसने ‘वर्मन’ उपसर्ग लिया, क्षत्रिय धर्म को किसी साफ–सुथरे दीक्षा–कर्म से नहीं, राजनीतिक दावा करके ओढ़ा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Banavasi with temples and administrative buildings growing, people of varied backgrounds moving through
panels.action: Banavasi now shows new temples, administrative halls, and bustling streets, farmers and traders mingling with scribes and soldiers as Mayurasharma oversees the town from a shaded veranda.

dialogue.text: Under him and his successors, Banavasi grew from a western outpost into a Kadamba capital, where Kannada country saw its own dynasty, no longer just a line in someone else’s grant.

i18n.hi: उसके समय और उत्तराधिकारियों में, बनवासी पश्चिमी चौकी से कदंब राजधानी बना, जहाँ कन्नड देश ने अपना खुद का वंश देखा, अब किसी दूसरे के दानपत्र की हाशिया-रेखा नहीं।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Mayurasharma’s weathered face to the Talagunda pillar inscription carved in stone centuries later
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s older, weathered face fades into the carved letters of the Talagunda pillar, standing alone among fields and trees, its surface worn but its script still sharp in the sun.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, his own descendants raised this pillar and sang of the scholar who drew a sword; it reminds us that hurt dignity can harden into fury, or, as in Mayurasharma’s case, into disciplined rule that reshaped a region.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, उसके ही वंशजों ने यह स्तंभ खड़ा किया और उस विद्वान की गाथा गाई, जिसने तलवार उठाई; यह बताता है कि चोटिल मान या तो अंधी हिंसा बनती है, या, मयूरशर्मा की तरह, अनुशासित राज, जो पूरे प्रदेश की रूपरेखा बदल दे।

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब कर्मकांड का हाथ बना हुकूमत का हाथ
